classification: Literal learned Illinois business-use exclusion conflicts with supplied benchmark statute and original TRAIN targets; three current EC misses align with wrong instruction, not just failure to execute a true rule

old_actual_EC_guidance.when: Illinois exemptions are allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property used personally rather than for business.
old_actual_EC_guidance.procedure: After classifying specific exemptions, make a separate § 12-1001(b) pass over every qualifying personal-property asset. Add 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) alongside any motor-vehicle, necessary-apparel or prescribed-health-aid citation, as well as for jewelry and other personal property. Its $4,000 ceiling limits protected equity, not EC eligibility.
old_actual_EC_guidance.avoid_when: Do not apply § 12-1001(b) to real property or property the facts explicitly identify as business-use. Do not omit it because a specific exemption applies, and do not classify jewelry as necessary wearing apparel.

teacher13_proposed_EC_guidance_not_yet_a.when: Illinois exemptions are allowable and the asset is debtor-owned personal property.
teacher13_proposed_EC_guidance_not_yet_a.procedure: Make a separate § 12-1001(b) pass over every such asset. Add 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) alongside every independently applicable paragraph (a), (c), (d), or (e), including for apparel, vehicles, jewelry, household goods, and trade tools. Its $4,000 ceiling limits protected equity, not EC eligibility.
teacher13_proposed_EC_guidance_not_yet_a.avoid_when: Do not apply § 12-1001(b) to real property or omit it because the asset has business use or another subsection applies. Under paragraph (a), jewelry is not necessary apparel and an electronic display is not itself a family picture; under paragraph (d), require stated trade use rather than treating a household appliance as a trade tool.
